verses.1: And David, an old man with seventy years of age, ruled over Solomon’s son in Israel.
verses.2: And he gathered all the elders of Israel, as well as the priests and the Levites.
verses.3: And the Levites were numbered from the age of thirty years and above. Their number amounted to three hundred and ten thousand.
verses.4: From these, there will be one hundred and forty-four thousand priests, judges, and officials.
verses.5: And four thousand doors, and four thousand people who praise the LORD with the instruments I made for worshiping Him.
verses.6: And David divided them into two groups: one group went to Gibeah, and the other group went to Meara.
verses.7: Help me to be strong and to hear.
verses.8: The sons of Ladan were Yehiel, Zetam, and Yoel, three in number.
verses.9: Shema’i’s sons: Shlomo, Hiziyael, and Haran. These three were the leaders of their fathers.
verses.10: And the sons of Shimei were Yachat Zina, Viyush, and Bria. These are the sons of Shimei: four in total.
verses.11: And then came the first child, and then the second. They worked hard, but their children didn’t grow too many. They became one family, but it was still a difficult situation for them.
verses.12: The sons of Kehat were Amram, Yizhar, Heveron, and Uzziel. There were four in total.
verses.13: The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart as holy, as being the most sacred among all people. He and his descendants were to be used as priests before Jehovah, to serve Him and to bless His name forever.
verses.14: And Moses, the man of God, would call upon his sons to stand on guard.
verses.15: The sons of Moses were Gershom and Eliezer.
verses.16: Children of Gershom, Shuvaeel the Rosh.
verses.17: And the sons of Eliezer were Rechbiyah and Rachbiyah. Eliezer had no other sons. And the number of children of Rechbiyah was very large.
verses.18: The sons of Yitzhar Shlomit Haraosh.
verses.19: The sons of Hivron were: Yeriyahu, the first; Amariah, the second; Yahziyael, the third; and Vikam’am, the fourth.
verses.20: The sons of Euziel were Michael the first, and Yishiyah the second.
verses.21: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushai. The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.
verses.22: And Elazar died, and he had no sons. All that remained of him were his daughters. And the sons of Kish took them as wives for their own children.
verses.23: The sons of Musi are Makhli, Edar, and Yiremot. There are three of them.
verses.24: These are the sons of Levi, who belong to their fathers. They are the heads of their families. They carry out the duties assigned to them in accordance with their names. They serve in the house of Jehovah since they were forty years old.
verses.25: For David said, “Let the LORD, the God of Israel, be with his people forever. Let him dwell in Jerusalem forever.”
verses.26: And even for the Levites, it is impossible to carry the tabernacle and all its contents into their service.
verses.27: For in the words of David, those who are mentioned are all sons of Levi, from the age of forty years onward.
verses.28: For they stand by the side of Aaron’s sons to serve in the Temple of Jehovah, on the courtyards and in the altars. They are also responsible for maintaining the sanctity of all sacred things and performing the rituals related to the Temple of God.
verses.29: And for the bread that is used as a meal, and for the desserts, and for the tables on which food is served, and for all kinds of dishes and utensils.
verses.30: And in the morning, stand up to pray and praise the LORD. The same goes for at night as well.
verses.31: And in all these ascents, we ascend to Jehovah for His Sabbaths, for new celebrations, and for festivals. As a law, this must always be done before Jehovah’s face.
verses.32: And they shall keep the laws regarding the sanctuary and the sacred things, as well as the laws regarding the descendants of Aaron, who were their brothers. They shall serve God’s house in accordance with these laws.
